response: Yes, implant retention can be recommended for the treatment of infected Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA), but with certain conditions. It is suggested that retention treatment can be selectively considered for non-S. aureus infections. Additionally, when applying this treatment, polyethylene exchange should be performed. Although the initial infection control rate may be lower in the retention group compared to the removal group, the final results can be comparable at the latest follow-up. Therefore, implant retention can be a viable option for treating infected TKA in selected patients.
